For customers that already have the technology (as informed by the “Technology Saturation” parameter), they do not have to pay the equipment and installation costs, but it is assumed that utilizing the flexibility features would still incur the annual operation and maintenance costs. Cost parameters shown are for 2019; 2030 costs are then estimated as a fraction of the 2019 costs according to the ratio shown in the table. Further, we also assume that the technology saturation increases with time. Hence, we use expected saturation values for the year 2030, which is also captured as part of the Phase 4 DR Potential Study. The technology lifetime is shown; this is used for annualizing the technology costs and assessing cost effectiveness. Finally, in the case of installing new technology on customer sites, we also incorporate the ability to finance the installation using a rate of 7%, consistent with the Phase 4 DR Potential Study. Technology cost and saturation assumptions The specific sources and documentation for each of these assumptions is available in the Phase 4 report appendix, but it should be noted that a primary source of these costs and saturation levels is the 2020 Grid-Interactive Efficient Building Technology Cost, Performance, 18 and Lifetime Characteristics report. Therefore, more recent technology developments and product offerings are not captured in these assumptions. Further, as noted, the majority of these technologies do not currently have hourly price response capabilities; it is unknown what the cost structure of these features will be, but an example is Nest thermostat’s Renew feature, which offers users a free option “to prioritize cleaner or less expensive energy”, or (at least, previously) offered a $10 per month premium subscription to match the user’s estimated demand with renewable energy credits16. For many devices, a large portion of the incremental cost for price response is to add communications capability and associated computational power. Many devices have communication added for reasons other than demand flexibility (e.g. LG adding Wi-Fi to all dishwasher models in 2018), at which point there is no additional hardware cost for flexibility. Some manufacturers may choose to include price response for free as a way to attract consumer attention. 2.5 Metrics for quantifying impacts of price response Customer bill impacts Customer bill impacts are a straightforward multiplication of the load impact and the price in each hour. If the load is increased in a given hour, the customer pays more, and if it is decreased, the customer saves accordingly. This calculation holds true as long as the hourly price represents the marginal volumetric charges the customer faces; in other words, the presence of a subscription would not impact the absolute value ($) of bill impacts.
